events.text: Restarting the private stack from clean state, then running all four probes.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Stop private stack by PID, clear state, restart
events.input: $ cd /tmp/t299 && for f in centre funnel runner sim; do p=$(cat $f.pid); pkill -TERM -P $p 2>/dev/null; kill $p 2>/dev/null; done; sleep 3; for f in centre funnel runner sim; do ps -p $(cat $f.pid) >/dev/null && echo "$f still up"; done; ps -ax -o pid,command | grep -E "port 89(30|34)|RUNNER_PORT|8931|8932" | grep -v grep | head; rm -rf state fstate sim.json d0 d1 d2; bash stack.sh > stack.out 2>&1; echo started

events.name: Bash
events.head: Wait for the private stack ports to answer
events.input: $ for i in $(seq 1 40); do c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8930/onboarding/); s=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8932/); f=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:8934/); [ "$c" != 000 ] && [ "$s" != 000 ] && [ "$f" != 000 ] && break; sleep 3; done; echo "$c $s $f"; tail -3 /tmp/t299/runner.log

events.name: Bash
events.head: Find the process holding runner port 8931
events.input: $ netstat -anv -p tcp | grep -E "\.8931 .*LISTEN" | head; ps -ax -o pid,ppid,command | grep local-runner | grep -v grep

events.name: Bash
events.head: Identify runner ports per process
events.input: $ for p in 1037 48927 65690; do echo "$p $(ps eww -p $p -o command= | grep -o 'RUNNER_PORT=[0-9]*') $(ps -p $p -o lstart=) cwd=$(ps -p $p -o command= >/dev/null; pwdx $p 2>/dev/null)"; done

events.text: The orphan on 8931 is an earlier T-299 runner; stopping it by PID and starting a fresh one.
